comment: Every key accepted in /etc/wsl.conf, the per-distribution file INSIDE a distribution. Not .wslconfig, which is the Windows-side file for the VM as a whole and has its own table. Read from src/linux/init/WslDistributionConfig.cpp:25-60, with defaults from WslDistributionConfig.h:57-86. Booleans accept true, false, 1 and 0, case-insensitively; yes, no, on and off are not accepted. Section and key names are matched case-insensitively, string values are not. Sections are never validated on their own: WSL joins section and key and looks up the whole name, so a bad section shows up as every key under it being unknown.

keys.desc: Mount the Windows drives under the automount root.
Where the Windows drives are mounted.
keys.note: An empty value becomes /, and a trailing slash is always added. Pointing this at an existing system directory such as /usr layers drive mounts over it, which is awkward to undo from inside the distribution.

keys.desc: Extra mount options for the Windows drives, for example metadata.
keys.note: Appended after WSL's own noatime, uid and gid, and applied only to automounted drive letters, not to /etc/fstab entries.

keys.desc: Process /etc/fstab when the distribution starts.
Write the Windows and GPU library search path and run ldconfig.
Which cgroup hierarchy is mounted at /sys/fs/cgroup.
keys.note: v1 is incompatible with per-distribution cgroup isolation, which recent WSL enables by default, and that conflict is only a warning. v1 also mounts a fresh tmpfs over /sys/fs/cgroup, which can leave systemd with a layout it did not expect. If the kernel command line disables cgroup v1, WSL falls back to v2 and only logs it.

keys.desc: umask applied to login sessions and the file server.
keys.note: Read as C would read it, so a leading zero means octal and a leading 0x means hexadecimal.

keys.desc: Allow running Windows executables from inside the distribution.
Put the Windows PATH on the end of the PATH inside the distribution.
keys.note: Independent of interop.enabled: interop can work with no Windows entries on PATH. Turning this off is a common cause of a Windows tool suddenly not being found from inside the distribution.

keys.desc: Let WSL write /etc/hosts.
Let WSL manage /etc/resolv.conf.
keys.note: With this off WSL also removes the symlink it previously created, and writes no replacement. If nothing else provides one you are left with no /etc/resolv.conf at all, which looks like name resolution working on Windows and not inside the distribution.

keys.desc: The hostname inside the distribution, instead of the Windows machine name.
Keep /etc/localtime in step with the Windows timezone.
Run the file server that backs \\wsl.localhost.
keys.note: Turning this off makes the distribution unreachable from Windows Explorer and from anything that reads its files over that path, including wslkit's own wsl.conf check.

keys.desc: Where the file server writes its log.
How much the file server logs, 0 to 5.
Truncate the file server log when the distribution starts.
Make the GPU driver share available inside the distribution.
Add the GPU library directory to the path.
The user a shell starts as.
keys.note: This beats the DefaultUid value in the Windows registry but never updates it, so the two drift apart and wsl --manage --set-default-user will appear not to have worked. Microsoft's own distribution validator discourages it for that reason. A username that does not exist falls back to the registry value, then to root.

keys.desc: Run systemd as the init inside the distribution.
keys.note: Forced off on WSL 1, and on WSL 2 if /sbin/init is not executable. A distribution built to assume systemd behaves oddly without it: systemctl reports that the system was not booted with systemd, and user sessions, socket activation and /run/user are all absent.

keys.desc: A command run as root when the distribution starts.
keys.note: Fire and forget: WSL does not wait for it and does not report its failure, so a mistake here looks like the distribution simply not working.

keys.desc: Milliseconds to wait for systemd to finish starting.
keys.note: Only meaningful with boot.systemd. A large value turns a distribution whose systemd never settles into an apparent hang on every wsl.exe call; zero skips the wait and hands you a half-started system.

keys.desc: Stop systemd's shutdown from clearing the interop handler for the whole VM.
keys.note: Only applied when boot.systemd is on. Turning it off can break running Windows executables from every distribution, not just this one.

keys.desc: Opt this distribution in or out of WSLg.
keys.note: WSL 2 only, and the VM-wide wsl2.guiApplications in .wslconfig has to be on as well.
